titles: How deep is the Mariana Trench, really?
Sinking 11 km to the bottom of the ocean
24.description:
A 50-second dive from the surface to Challenger Deep, about 10,935 metres down, through every zone of the ocean: the light running out, the pressure climbing past 1,000 atmospheres, and the animals that live at each depth.

Sources:
- Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m deep: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceandepth.html
- Ocean zones and their depths: https://www.whoi.edu/ocean-learning-hub/ocean-topics/how-the-ocean-works/ocean-zones/
- Deepest fish ever filmed, a snailfish at 8,336 m: https://uwa.edu.au/news/Article/2023/April/Scientists-break-new-record-after-finding-worlds-deepest-fish

titles: What if you fell into a hole through the Earth?
Falling through the centre of the Earth
30.description:
Someone dug a hole straight through the planet and you tripped in. A 55-second fall past the deepest mine and the deepest hole ever drilled, through the mantle and the liquid-iron outer core, to a centre as hot as the Sun's surface, and out the other side.

Sources:
- Mponeng, the deepest mine, is over 4 km deep with rock at 66 °C: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mponeng_Gold_Mine
- Deepest mine (Guinness World Records): https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/66169-deepest-mine
- Kola Superdeep Borehole reached 12,262 m in 1989 after drilling began in 1970: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kola_Superdeep_Borehole
- The mantle's rock flows slowly over geological time: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth%27s_mantle
- The liquid-iron outer core starts about 2,900 km down and drives Earth's magnetic field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth%27s_outer_core
- Inner core pressure is about 330–360 GPa: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth%27s_inner_core
- The centre of the Earth is about as hot as the Sun's surface (Anzellini et al. 2013): https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/the-center-of-the-earth-is-as-hot-as-the-sun-43631207
- A fall through the Earth takes about 38 minutes 11 seconds, reaching over 8 km/s (Klotz 2015): https://www.livescience.com/50312-how-long-to-fall-through-earth.html

Sound effects:
- "JET WHOOSH LOW" by sound.variant (https://freesound.org/people/sound.variant/sounds/807291/), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), edited

titles: What if you started floating up and couldn't stop?
Floating from the ground to the Space Station
32.description:
One morning you start floating straight up. A 50-second rise past Everest, airliners, the Armstrong limit, Felix Baumgartner's record jump and the edge of space, all the way to the Space Station, and why the air up there is over 1,000 degrees but would still freeze you.

Sources:
- Everest is 8,849 m tall, with about a third of sea-level air pressure at the summit: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Everest
- Air at airliner cruising altitude (11 km) is about −56 °C in the standard atmosphere: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Standard_Atmosphere
- The Armstrong limit (about 18–19 km), where water boils at body temperature: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armstrong_limit
- Felix Baumgartner jumped from 38,969 m on 14 October 2012 and reached Mach 1.25: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Stratos
- The Kármán line at 100 km is the commonly used edge of space: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%A1rm%C3%A1n_line
- The thermosphere can be extremely hot yet would feel very cold: https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/thermosphere/en/
- The Space Station orbits about 400 km up, circling Earth about every 90 minutes: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station
- If Earth were an apple, the atmosphere would be as thick as its skin: https://scied.ucar.edu/activity/atmospheric-layers

Sound effects:

titles: What if you poured all of Earth's water into one ball?
Earth is 71% ocean, but has surprisingly little water
34.description:
A spin around the globe from the Pacific to Lake Baikal, ending with every drop of Earth's water squeezed into a single ball.

Sources:
- About 71% of Earth's surface is ocean; 96.5% of Earth's water is in the oceans; 2.5% is fresh water, 68.7% of it in glaciers: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_distribution_on_Earth
- The Pacific covers more than 30% of Earth's surface and is larger than all the continents combined: https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/ocean-fact/pacific-size/
- Average ocean depth about 3,682 m; Challenger Deep about 10,935 m: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceandepth.html
- Lake Baikal contains 20% of the world's total unfrozen fresh water: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/754
- All the water on Earth would form a sphere about 860 miles (about 1,385 km) across: https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/all-water-earth-a-sphere-placed-over-a-dry-globe

titles: What if you sank all the way down to the Titanic?
Sinking 3.8 km to the Titanic, and what's eating it
36.description:
Sink from the surface of the North Atlantic through the sunlight, twilight and midnight zones to the wreck of the Titanic, 3,800 metres down, and meet the rust-eating bacterium slowly destroying it.

Sources:
- The wreck lies about 3,800 m (12,500 ft) down, in two main pieces about 600 m apart: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic_wreck
- The Titanic sank on 15 April 1912; the bow hit the bottom at about 20 knots (10 m/s): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic_wreck
- Water at the wreck is about 1-2 °C; Mann and Kaur's analysis says the wreck will not exist by 2037: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic_wreck
- The upper 200 m is the sunlight zone; below 1,000 m sunlight does not penetrate: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/light_travel.html
- Pressure rises by one atmosphere for every 10.06 m (33 ft) of depth, so about 380 atm at 3,800 m: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/pressure.html
- A new rust-eating bacterium found in the Titanic's rusticles was named Halomonas titanicae: https://www.livescience.com/9079-species-rust-eating-bacteria-destroying-titanic.html

titles: How big is the biggest star? (it's not the Sun)
From the Moon to UY Scuti, to scale
43.description:
A to-scale zoom out from the Moon to Earth, Jupiter, the Sun, Betelgeuse and UY Scuti, one of the largest known stars: about 909 times wider than the Sun.

Sources:
- The Moon is about 3,475 km across: https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/
- Earth's equatorial diameter is 12,756 km: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/
- Jupiter's radius is 69,911 km; about 1,000 Earths would fit inside it: https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/facts/
- The Sun is about 1.4 million km wide; about 1.3 million Earths would fill it: https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/
- Betelgeuse's radius is about 764 solar radii (Joyce et al. 2020); at the Sun's position it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betelgeuse
- Mars orbits at about 1.52 AU (so its orbit is about 456 million km across): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars
- UY Scuti's radius is about 909 solar radii (2023); its volume is about 750 million times the Sun's; it may not be the largest known star: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UY_Scuti
